concept.name: Evening star
concept.definition: A three-candlestick top reversal pattern: a long white body is followed by a small-bodied candle (the star, of either color) that gaps above the first body, and then a long black body that closes well into the first candle's real body. Technical analysts treat it as a major top reversal signal marking a shift from buying to indecision to selling; it is the bearish mirror of the morning star.
concept.intuition: Buyers push hard, then the market stalls in a small indecisive candle near the highs, then sellers seize control and erase much of the advance, like nightfall after a bright day.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long white body in an uptrend; candle 2 has a small real body (ideally gapping above body 1); candle 3 is a long black body closing below the midpoint of body 1. Classic definitions want gaps around the star; these are commonly relaxed in gap-poor markets.
concept.failure_modes: In strong bull trends the third candle's dip is often bought, and the uptrend resumes. In 24-hour markets without gaps, loosely matched 'evening stars' generate many false tops.
concept.misconceptions: The star candle can be either color and need not be a doji (a doji star makes it an evening doji star). The signal is only conventionally valid once the third candle has closed deep into the first body.
concept.example: A stock climbs, printing a long white candle (70.00 to 72.00), then a tiny-bodied candle around 72.30-72.50, then a long black candle closing at 70.50. The evening star is read as a top reversal warning.
